column1: # *** THE DGS AUDIT - every film number in the archive tested, 20 September 2026. ***
# Row 40 held that any DGS taken from a catalogue rather than from opening the film was suspect,
# because two Montevideo attributions had already failed inspection. *** All 58 were tested. ***
# *** The suspicion is cleared: not one DGS in this archive points at a film that does not exist. ***
# It was done with FamilySearch SIGNED OUT, which is the point of the method.

column2: *** 58 numbers cited explicitly as DGS. 57 resolve to a real film. 1 exists but is access-restricted at every image tested. NOT FOUND: zero. ***
column3: *** Row 40 is answered and the answer is that the archive's film numbers are sound. *** Each was tested at three images - 1, 100 and 500 - rather than one, because a single probe cannot tell a missing film from a restricted page.

column1: *** THE METHOD, AND WHY IT WORKS SIGNED OUT ***
column2: *** thumb_p200.jpg is PUBLIC *** - plain curl fetches it with no session: /service/records/storage/deepzoomcloud/dz/v1/dgs:{film9}.{film9}_{image5}/thumb_p200.jpg
column3: *** So a film number can be verified while FamilySearch search is signed out entirely ***, which is how this was done. *** CORRECTION TO THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN NOTE: manifest.json is NOT public. *** It answers *** 401 'Unauthorized (anonymous session)' *** to an unauthenticated request, so the manifest route needs a session and the thumbnail route does not.

column1: *** TRAP ONE: 401 DOES NOT MEAN THE FILM IS WRONG ***
column2: On DGS 008166573, image 1 returns *** 401 ***, image 100 returns *** 200 ***, image 500 returns *** 401 *** and image 2167 returns *** 200. *** One film, both answers.
column3: *** Access is set PER IMAGE, not per film. *** A 401 means that page is restricted; *** only a 404 means the film is not there. *** Probing image 1 alone and reading its 401 as a bad number would have produced a false correction against a film that is demonstrably fine. *** The bogus control 999999999 returns 404 ***, which is how the two are told apart.

column1: *** TRAP TWO, AND IT CAUGHT ME ***
column2: The first pass matched *** film *** as well as *** DGS *** and reported *** six failures ***: 001091419, 001091422, 002124160, 002124219, 002124260, 002274694.
column3: *** ALL SIX ARE OLD MICROFILM ROLL NUMBERS AND ALL SIX ARE CORRECTLY LABELLED. *** The archive writes *** 'DGS 7713373 (film 2124160, items 5-13)' *** and *** 'DGS 8166578, items 11-13 (old film 2274694)' *** - the DGS beside the old roll number, exactly as it should. *** The fault was in my regex, not in the data ***, and an old microfilm number is not addressable by DeepZoom at all. *** Six false corrections avoided by reading the citation before believing the test. ***

column2: *** DGS 008166571 *** returned 401 at images 1, 100 and 500. Cited in ark-to-film.tsv, canelones-1776-1794.tsv and sancho-children-reconciled.tsv.
column3: *** Restricted, not wrong - and not proven either. *** No 200 was obtained anywhere on it, so unlike 008166573 there is no positive proof the film is what the archive says. *** Left as the single open item of this audit ***, to be settled by one signed-in fetch when a session exists.
